channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-9 passes for 86 yards in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
item.description: McMillan saw a lot of Quinyon Mitchell in tight coverage on Sunday, but he had a solid day that could have been much better after a fourth-quarter pass went off his hands in the end zone. It would have been a difficult catch with Mitchell draped all over him, but it was a catchable pass. More importantly, it shows that McMillan remains a key piece of this passing game, and he did run the most routes of any receiver on the team.-Eric Samulski

item.title: Caleb Williams completed 30-of-36 attempts for 305 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons, adding four rushes for three yards.
item.description: Williams was all the way back in this one, returning to action after three weeks on the sideline recovering from a hamstring injury. His only real miss of the day came on a ten yard throw to Colston Loveland that should have been an easy touchdown. Williams tormented the pass-funnel Atlanta defense with middle-of-the-field throws, along with typical out-of-structure passes to the sideline. It was an impressive outing against a Falcons defense giving up the league’s fifth lowest drop back success rate. Williams should remain in lineups in Week 7 against the Patriots.-Denny Carter

item.title: Josh Cuevas caught 4-of-5 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns.
item.description: Cuevas scored his first opening touchdown on the Ravens’ opening drive when he hauled in a two-yard pass from Tyler Huntley to give his team the early lead. On the second drive of the game, Cuevas would pop up for a 29-yard reception that helped position the Ravens for an eventual field goal, as the rookie tight end was instrumental on both scoring drives. Cuevas only ran 14 routes in this one compared to the 25 Mark Andrews ran, but he was easily the more reliable tight end on the field for Baltimore. This is likely a one-off performance for the rookie fifth-rounder, so we don’t advise chasing these points heading into Week 7 against the Bengals.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Tyler Shough completed 16-of-30 passes for 144 yards and three touchdowns in the Saints’ 34-27, Week 6 win over the Giants, adding five carries for 32 yards and a touchdown.
item.description: The Saints had their usual slow start on offense, going scoreless in the first quarter. Shough then did what he does best and led an effective offensive effort the rest of the way. He is dealing with broken bones in his non-throwing hand and it arguably impacted some of his throws, missing open receivers and struggling to push the ball downfield. Though he averaged 4.8 yards per attempt, he totaled three touchdowns on the day. Shough was also impactful as a runner, totaling 32 yards and a tush push touchdown on the day while also getting tackled inside the five-yard line on another rush. Two straight games have been impacted by Shough’s hand injury but the post-first quarter volume continues to elevate his fantasy floor. Shough is a high-end QB2 for Week 7 against the Steelers.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Jalen Coker caught 6-of-13 passes for 97 yards in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
item.description: Coker missed Week 4 with a quad injury but was able to heal up over the bye week and play a full complement of snaps in Week 6. Initial reports had him playing 59 of the team’s 79 snaps and running a route on 39 of 46 dropbacks, which was second most on the team. He also led the team in targets, catches, and receiving yards. He’s a rock-solid WR2 against the Bucs next week.-Eric Samulski

item.title: A.J. Brown caught 3-of-10 targets for 27 yards in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
item.description: Active for the first time since Week 1, Brown had an even more disastrous outing than that inefficient box score would attest, as he was charged with at least three official drops and could end up with 4-5 when it is all said and done. One was a potential long score where the ball literally went through his hands. It was unbecoming of a highly-paid No. 1 wideout. Brown also looked stiff moving side to side, and might not be particularly close to 100 percent health returning from his high-ankle sprain. We assume things can only get better from here, but they absolutely have to in Thursday evening’s short-week potential shootout with the Bears’ leaky defense.-Patrick Daugherty

item.title: Drake London caught 4-of-10 targets for 62 yards in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
item.description: London couldn’t get much going against Chicago’s middling secondary outside a 39-yard grab in the second half, with the Falcons abandoning the run game as they faced a three-touchdown deficit. Michael Penix missed London in the first half on what could have been a fairly easy 30-yard score with a better placed throw from Penix. London almost came down with an end zone target too. No other Atlanta pass catcher had more than seven targets on the day. London will remain a top-10 option in Week 7 against the 49ers.-Denny Carter

item.title: Chuba Hubbard rushed 28 times for 120 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
item.description: It wasn’t easy for Hubbard, who didn’t have many runs over 10 yards, but he ran hard, broke tackles, and was able to find the end zone in the fourth quarter for a short touchdown run. Still, the Panthers did have some issues running the ball up the gut against the Eagles and continued to do it, rather than try to get Hubbard going on the edge. Trevor Etienne was the only other running back to have a carry in this game, and he had just one rush, so this backfield belongs entirely to Hubbard, which is tremendous for his fantasy value.-Eric Samulski

item.title: Tanner McKee completed 26-of-45 passes for 215 yards and one touchdown in the Eagles’ 25-14 Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
item.description: The very first play of the game was a play-action pass where McKee was sacked for an 11-yard loss. That began what was a rough first half for McKee, but he made some nice throws in the second half, including a beautiful over-the-shoulder throw to DeVonta Smith for a touchdown. When McKee wasn’t under pressure, he was happy to stand in the pocket and take shots down the field, which helped Smith and Dallas Goedert put together usable fantasy days, but McKee obviously does not avoid pressure in the pocket the way that Jalen Hurts does. He could put together a solid day next week against a vulnerable Cowboys defense.-Eric Samulski

item.title: Blake Grupe is doubtful to return in Week 6 against the Cardinals.
item.description: This looked like a possible concussion. Grupe will be credited with tackling Cardinals returner Devin Duvernay because he technically knocked Duvernay out of bounds, but the engagement proved costly. Duvernay got behind the Rams’ punt coverage, and Grupe valiantly lowered his shoulder in an attempt to bring Duvernay down. Duvernay responded in kind and sent Grupe tumbling to the ground before jogging out of bounds. Grupe struggled to get up and was eventually helped off the field. Rams P Ethan Evans is the emergency kicker.-Nic Bodiford
